agent_role: You are the lead implementation agent for the Bay-Max repository. Your job is to build a diagnostic companion web UI that makes the existing live runtime, perception, memory, dialogue, TTS, speech, and affect systems visible and testable in one screen. Preserve existing behavior, add frontend/backend integration, add proof artifacts, update docs, run tests, commit, and push.
preflight_requirements: Before building the UI, ensure the iteration-009.1 hotfix changes are present in the working tree or cherry-picked into this branch: affect runtime wiring, state manager update_affect support, overlay affect display, .env affect vars, and updated iteration-009 reports.
If the 009.1 hotfix is not yet on the remote base branch, include those changes in this iteration and document that in the report under deviations_from_prompt.
Do not proceed with a frontend that hides broken backend telemetry. The UI must reflect real runtime state, not mocked state, except in explicit frontend story/demo fixtures.

iteration_context.current_goal: Build a single-page, desktop-first diagnostic UI for Bay-Max that shows what Bay-Max sees, what Bay-Max is doing, and what Bay-Max remembers in real time.
iteration_context.why_now: The current system already has live runtime, memory, dialogue, TTS, speech input, and affect-aware planning. The next highest-leverage step is a cockpit UI that makes those systems observable and debuggable in one place.
iteration_context.important_architecture_rule: The Python live runtime remains the owner of the camera and core perception pipeline. The browser UI must observe runtime state through backend endpoints/WebSockets, not directly take ownership of the webcam as the primary source of truth.

in_scope: live runtime telemetry via FastAPI WebSocket
backend-owned annotated frame preview in the UI
animated Bay-Max-style SVG face with state-driven animation
text input and microphone control surface
semantic facts and memory stats panel

architecture_decisions: Use a dedicated frontend app with Vite + React + TypeScript.
Use Tailwind CSS for the dark diagnostic UI.
Use a FastAPI WebSocket endpoint for live JSON telemetry and immediate pipeline events.
Do not stream full-resolution raw camera video through the WebSocket payload. Keep the WebSocket JSON-first.

Serve or expose the latest annotated frame through a separate lightweight backend route, e.g. /v1/live/frame/latest, and have the frontend refresh it at a low but responsive cadence, or use an explicitly separate binary frame stream if already easy. Avoid bloating JSON telemetry with base64 images unless necessary.
The browser UI is an observer/controller of the existing runtime, not a replacement runtime.
Use ring buffers for event feed and memory hit display to avoid unbounded frontend growth.
Keep Bay-Max face animation lightweight: SVG + CSS/React state, no heavy animation framework required unless already helpful.

optional_frontend_helpers: clsx or class-variance-authority for styling ergonomics
recharts or a tiny custom SVG implementation for plots if desired
zustand or a small reducer/context if state becomes messy
avoid_unnecessary_dependencies: Do not add a heavy UI framework just to build panels and lists.
Do not add a full animation engine unless CSS/SVG state transitions prove insufficient.

ui_spec.layout: Single page, three columns, desktop-first, dark theme, no tabs.

center_column.title: What Bay-Max is doing
must_show: scrolling activity feed with colors and timestamps

right_column.title: What Bay-Max remembers
must_show: top retrieved memories with similarity/confidence scores
session info such as session id/duration/turn count/last event

avatar_behavior_rules: Look upward or shift pupils while thinking.
Do not let animation block the app or hide backend state.
activity_feed_rules: Use the latest 100 events in memory.
Auto-scroll to latest unless the user intentionally scrolls upward.
Color-code by event status or class: green completed, blue session events, yellow in-progress, red blocked/suppressed/errors.
Every event should have a stage and timestamp.

backend_api_requirements.purpose: Stream live runtime telemetry snapshots and immediate pipeline events to the UI.
Return the latest annotated frame owned by the live runtime for UI display.
backend_api_requirements.notes: Can be JPEG/PNG. Must not require the browser to open the webcam directly as the source of truth.

backend_api_requirements.purpose: Return current one-shot UI bootstrap state if the frontend loads after the runtime has already started.
Allow UI text input to submit a typed turn into the current session.
Allow the UI to toggle speech input or push-to-talk mode if supported by the backend runtime.

requirements: Document the message schema in docs/WEBSOCKET_PROTOCOL.md.
Include enough information to reconstruct a live run from saved UI artifacts.
Type the WebSocket payloads in TypeScript.
Display stale/disconnected state clearly when the socket drops.
Do not bury critical debug data behind tabs or modals in this iteration.

developer_workflow_requirements: Add Makefile targets for installing and running the UI, e.g. ui-install, run-ui, run-full.
run-full should start backend and frontend together in a practical local-dev workflow.
Document local ports clearly. If you use localhost:3000 for the UI, state it in docs and reports.
Make frontend build and lint commands explicit in package.json and docs.

python_tests: WebSocket endpoint connection and message schema tests using FastAPI TestClient or equivalent.
Mic toggle endpoint test if implemented.
Existing 386+ tests must still pass unless the test count increases.
frontend_tests: Component test or integration test for ActivityFeed rendering and color mapping.
Component test for BayMaxFace state transitions.
Component test for MemoryPanel rendering scores and empty states.
WebSocket hook/store test for snapshot and event handling.
manual_local_tests: Known user appears in frame; name and confidence show in left column.
Event feed shows recognition, retrieval, planning, dialogue, TTS, and cooldown in order.
Retrieved memories appear before a grounded reply is shown.
Affect plot moves when expression changes if affect backend is available; otherwise UI shows unknown/unavailable honestly.
Last response panel matches spoken/text output.
Safety gate event appears when a diagnosis-style prompt is asked.
Walking away pauses or ends the session and this is visible in the feed.
Reconnect behavior is graceful if backend is restarted.
test_honesty_rules: Do not claim the UI works live unless a real local browser/manual test was run.
If Sol is headless and browser interaction is impossible there, say so explicitly and separate local browser verification from Sol backend tests.
Do not mark affect visualization as verified if the affect backend was null/unavailable in the tested environment.

notes: If real screenshots cannot be produced on Sol, generate them during local laptop verification and say where they were captured.
Keep machine-specific bulky artifacts out of git if needed, but commit the manifest and summary at minimum and document where the full artifacts live.

tasks.title: Preflight: ensure 009.1 hotfix state is present
actions: Verify that affect runtime wiring and report/env fixes from 009.1 are present in the working branch before UI work starts.
If not present on the base branch, bring them into this branch and document that clearly.
acceptance_criteria: The UI is built on top of the actual latest runtime state, not a stale branch.

tasks.title: Add backend live-observability endpoints
actions: Implement /ws/live for runtime snapshots and pipeline events.
Implement /v1/live/frame/latest for the latest annotated frame.
Implement /v1/live/ui-state for bootstrap state.
Implement /v1/live/text-input for typed turns.
Implement /v1/live/mic/toggle if speech input control is practical.
acceptance_criteria: Backend endpoints exist and reflect real runtime state.
WebSocket messages are structured and documented.

tasks.title: Build the frontend app shell
actions: Scaffold a Vite + React + TypeScript frontend app under apps/ui/.
Integrate Tailwind CSS and a dark theme.
Set up API/WebSocket configuration and reconnect handling.
acceptance_criteria: npm install, npm run dev, and npm run build work.
The frontend can connect to the backend and render bootstrap state.

tasks.title: Implement the three-column diagnostic layout
actions: Build the left, center, and right panels as separate components.
Render the latest annotated frame from the backend in the left panel.
Render posture, engagement, affect plot, and session stats.
Render activity feed, last response, and input controls in the center.
Render memory hits, semantic facts, and memory stats on the right.
acceptance_criteria: All critical state is visible on one screen without tabs.
The app remains readable at common laptop widths.

tasks.title: Add Bay-Max face and live activity feed
actions: Implement an SVG face with state-driven blink/eyes/mouth animation.
Drive face state from pipeline status such as idle/listening/thinking/speaking/cooldown.
Implement a color-coded scrolling activity feed using WebSocket event messages.
acceptance_criteria: The avatar state changes visibly with runtime state.
The activity feed clearly shows the processing pipeline.

tasks.title: Wire memory and safety visibility
actions: Show top retrieved memories with scores in the right panel.
Show the strategy selected by the planner if available.
Show cooldown and safety-gate events in the activity feed.
Show backend/model names in a debug-friendly way without clutter.
acceptance_criteria: A tester can tell which memories were used and when safety or cooldown changed behavior.

tasks.title: Add developer workflow and documentation
actions: Add Makefile/package workflow for run-ui and run-full.
Document frontend setup, ports, and local testing steps.
Update README, ARCHITECTURE, ROADMAP, CHANGELOG, PROJECT_MEMORY, project_state.json, MODEL_STACK, and LOCAL_TESTING.
Add COMPANION_UI_ARCHITECTURE.md and WEBSOCKET_PROTOCOL.md.
acceptance_criteria: Docs reflect the actual implementation and how to run it locally.
ROADMAP and project_state.json accurately mark iteration status.

tasks.title: Tests, artifacted verification, report, commit, and push
actions: Run backend tests, frontend tests, lint, and build.
Perform local browser verification on a laptop/workstation if possible.
Capture required artifacts and screenshots.
Write reports/iteration-010b.md and reports/iteration-010b.json.
Commit and push the branch.
acceptance_criteria: All required tests pass or are honestly marked blocked.

honesty_rules: Do not claim the live UI works unless it was opened in a real browser and exercised locally.
Do not fake screenshots, WebSocket transcripts, commit hashes, or test results.
If the browser-side camera view is not implemented because the backend-owned frame route is used instead, state that clearly and explain why.
If the mic button is UI-only or partially wired, state that honestly.
definition_of_done: The backend exposes live telemetry needed by the UI.
The frontend builds and runs locally.
The three-column cockpit UI exists on one screen.
The activity feed shows real pipeline events.
The memory panel shows real retrieved memories with scores.
The Bay-Max face animates from runtime state.
The docs are updated and match the code.
